renders._yaml:
- component: figure
  id: telomere_length_bar
  title: Telomere length per sample
  description: |-
    Each bar is the telomere length TEAL estimates for a DNA sample, adjusted for tumor purity, coloured by sample type. It answers how long the telomeres are and whether the tumor differs from its normal.
    How to read: a tumor far above its normal suggests telomerase or ALT activity, and a tumor far below it suggests telomere attrition. Compare each tumor with its own reference sample.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/teal/README.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sampleId
    y: finalTelomereLength
    color: type
    labels:
      sampleId: Sample
      finalTelomereLength: Telomere length (bp)
      type: Sample type

- component: card
  id: telomere_length_spread
  title: Telomere length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median final telomere length over the DNA samples, with the shortest and longest beside it. It answers how long the telomeres are across the run.
    How to read: tumor and reference samples sit in one table, so read the range together with the bar chart to see which sample is at each end. A tumor with a length far from its normal is the finding.
    Note: the final length is adjusted for purity and ploidy for tumor samples and equals the raw length for the reference.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/teal/README.md
  column: finalTelomereLength
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: median, with its range
  headline: true

- component: table
  id: telomere_table
  title: Telomere length estimates
  description: |-
    Each row is a DNA sample with its raw and final telomere length, the telomeric fragments behind it and the purity, ploidy and read depth used to normalise it. It answers how reliable each estimate is.
    How to read: an estimate on few telomeric reads or at low purity is less certain, so check the fragment counts before comparing samples.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/teal/README.md
